slides.say: The third tool is a trapezoid inside a circle. When a trapezoid is inscribed in a circle, it's always an isosceles trapezoid. Let's see why, with two rules we already know.
at: The third tool is a trapezoid

slides.say: Here's trapezoid A B C D, inscribed in a circle. A B is parallel to D C. Say angle A is seventy.
at: A B is parallel to D C

slides.say: First, the trapezoid rule. Two angles on the same leg add up to one hundred eighty. Angles A and D are both on the leg A D. So angle D is one hundred eighty minus seventy, which is one hundred ten.
at: So angle D is one hundred eighty minus
So angle D is one hundred eighty minus

slides.say: Now the circle rule. In an inscribed quadrilateral, opposite angles add up to one hundred eighty. Angle C is opposite angle A. So angle C is one hundred eighty minus seventy, which is one hundred ten too.
at: So angle C is one hundred eighty minus
So angle C is one hundred eighty minus

slides.say: So angle C and angle D are equal, and they're the two angles on the base D C. Angle B is on the same leg as C, so it's one hundred eighty minus one hundred ten, which is seventy. That's the same as angle A. So the base angles are equal on both bases.
at: minus one hundred ten, which is seventy

slides.say: And equal base angles give equal legs. Drop the heights from D and from C to the base A B. We get two right triangles with the same height and the same angle of seventy at the bottom. So they're the same triangle, and their long sides are equal. Those long sides are the legs A D and B C. So the trapezoid is isosceles.
at: Those long sides are the legs

slides.say: Seventy was just an example. Say angle A is sixty-four. Then angle D is one hundred sixteen, because it's on the same leg as A. And angle C is one hundred sixteen too, because it's opposite A. They're equal again, for any angle.
at: Then angle D is one hundred sixteen

slides.say: So when a question says a trapezoid is inscribed in a circle, you know right away that it's isosceles. Its legs are equal, its base angles are equal, and its diagonals are equal too. And a trapezoid with unequal legs can never be inscribed in a circle. Now let's see the other two tools in questions, and I'll see you in the next video.
